newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank raises chemical stocks to buy.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank raises chemical stocks to buy.

text.p: Commerzbank AG, Germany's third largest commercial bank, said on Thursday it had upgraded Hoechst AG, BASF AG and Bayer AG to "buy" as the chemical industry shares were breaking out of a long phase of underperformance.
Analyst Gerrit Jost noted that BASF and Bayer had risen only 23 percent this year and Hoechst just 20 percent compared with a 48 percent gain on the DAX.
"We do not consider underperformance to this extent to be justified and expect above average price developments in the coming months," Jost said in a report.
The bank had previously had "hold" recommendations on Bayer and Hoechst and a "sell" recommendation on BASF.
Jost said the appreciation of the dollar, and of the pound sterling, enhanced earnings prospects for the German chemical firms in the current year and next year.
Also there was strong potential in the global pharmaceutical industry because of the outlook for growth and a process of concentration in the sector.
Prices for specialty chemicals firms and their share prices had also risen considerably, he noted.

Commerzbank raised its EPS estimates for 1997 and 1998 for all three companies. The bank raised its EPS estimate for Hoechst to 3.45 marks per share this year from 3.30 marks and to 4.10 marks next year from four marks.
It raised Bayer's EPS estimate for 1997 to 4.25 marks from four marks and the estimate for 1998 to 4.40 marks from 4.20 marks.
For BASF, the bank upped its 1997 EPS forecast to 4.95 marks from 4.70 marks and the 1998 forecast to 5.05 marks from 4.80 marks.
